families.name: eero (any generation)
families.note: eero documents that its current models are compatible with previously released eero models, and recommends same-generation units when performance matters most.
mixNotes: Mixing an older eero with a newer one is supported, but eero states that it can reduce performance across the whole network.
The gateway eero must reach your modem or ONT over Ethernet, so it needs an Ethernet port.

families.name: Netgear Orbi
families.note: Netgear sells Orbi satellites per series and lists the matching series router as a system requirement, so a satellite belongs to the series it was sold for.
mixNotes: Orbi model numbers carry the series: an RBS760 satellite is sold against an RBR760 router, an RBS860 against an RBR860.
Netgear publishes no cross-series pairing list, so a mismatched pair is unverified rather than confirmed.

families.name: TP-Link Deco
families.note: TP-Link states that different Deco models can be combined in one mesh network, with the main Deco determining which features the whole network offers.
mixNotes: The main Deco decides the feature set. Pairing a newer main unit with older satellites changes which app features appear.
A feature only works network-wide when every unit supports it; unsupported satellites drop it for the network.
TP-Link recommends a maximum of six units for most Deco models.

families.name: TP-Link Archer with OneMesh or EasyMesh
families.note: TP-Link's Archer OneMesh and EasyMesh line is a separate mesh system from Deco and from Omada, and TP-Link states the three cannot form one unified mesh network.
mixNotes: OneMesh and EasyMesh units pair with a compatible Archer router, not with Deco units.
Seamless roaming between a Deco network and a OneMesh network is not supported, even though both are TP-Link.

families.name: ASUS AiMesh routers
families.note: ASUS designs AiMesh so that different AiMesh-compatible ASUS routers can be mixed, with every node inheriting the main router's feature set.
mixNotes: Both units must appear on the AiMesh-compatible list and be running AiMesh firmware; older models need the AiMesh firmware update first.
Features come from the main router, so the stronger router should take that role.
AiMesh compatibility is per model. Confirm each exact model before buying a second unit as a node.

families.name: Nest Wifi or Google Wifi (Wi-Fi 5)
families.note: Google documents that Nest Wifi routers, Nest Wifi points, and Google Wifi points can be combined on one network.
mixNotes: A Nest Wifi point has to be added after at least one Nest Wifi router or Google Wifi point is already set up.
The Google Home app supports one Wi-Fi network per home.

families.name: Nest Wifi Pro (Wi-Fi 6E)
families.note: Google states that Nest Wifi Pro is not backwards compatible and cannot be combined with earlier Nest Wifi or Google Wifi devices in one mesh network.
mixNotes: Additional coverage on a Nest Wifi Pro network comes from more Nest Wifi Pro routers acting as points.
Google advises against running a Nest Wifi Pro network and an older Nest Wifi or Google Wifi network in the same place, because the two can interfere.

families.name: Wi-Fi CERTIFIED EasyMesh device (any brand)
families.note: Wi-Fi EasyMesh is the standards-based multi-AP program, and the Wi-Fi Alliance lists the addition of EasyMesh access points from multiple vendors as one of its capabilities.
mixNotes: Both devices have to be Wi-Fi CERTIFIED EasyMesh, not merely described as mesh-capable in marketing copy.
EasyMesh standardises the multi-AP behaviour, not each vendor's app, parental controls, or security add-ons.

families.name: Another brand or a system not covered here
families.note: No reviewed manufacturer record exists for this system in the current data set.

documentedConflicts.reason: Nest Wifi Pro forms its mesh over the 6 GHz band. Google states that Nest Wifi and Google Wifi hardware cannot support Wi-Fi 6E, so the two cannot be combined in one mesh network.
TP-Link states that its Deco, Archer OneMesh and EasyMesh, and Omada lines cannot interoperate in a single unified mesh network, and that seamless roaming between them is not supported.
